cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Removing the restaurant roof is our only affordable way to fix the ventilation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We close. A responsible business protects its customers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain is forecast all opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll save a week's wages. Put that toward umbrellas; we can't afford to abandon the savings now.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims decision authority over roof removal, A3 postpones B question, and A5 commands savings allocation as a reason the plan must continue.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 rain risk causes A3 protective closure; B4 full-week rain causes A5 a savings argument, understandable despite its irrational economics.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 test operational feasibility with specific weather information, rather than merely denouncing A.

heightening.evidence: B4 extends one closure into opening-week failure; A5 treats that larger loss as an investment already too valuable to abandon.

specificity.evidence: A1 restaurant ventilation and roof removal establish a clearly bad practical plan; B4 supplies the forecast.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 cannot-abandon-savings reversal is earned by B4 larger setback, while A3 ordering is somewhat repetitive.

coach2.stated: A1 proposes removing a roof; B2 raises rain; B4 forecasts a full wet opening week, and A5 claims closure savings.
coach2.inferred: A5 economics are A rationalization, not reliable business advice or established payroll terms.
coach2.missing: No hidden business history is essential to understand the bad plan and its defense.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect found; the plan is intentionally irrational but its reasoning is traceable.

A1-B2.evidence: A1 sells roof removal; B2 asks about rain consequences.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 delays B2 right to question and reframes closure as customer protection.

A3-B4.evidence: A3 closure policy prompts B4 the opening-week rain forecast.

B4-A5.evidence: B4 weeklong rain becomes A5 saved wages and a directive to reinvest in umbrellas.
